facts: When entering the zone of gate mark 3p, AUS 216366 as outside of two unidntified boats, all on port tack and overlapped bow to bow.
IRL 211114 also on port tack 1 m clear astern of these three boats.
At the mark AUS 216366 and two unidentified boats luffed and broke the overlap and lined up bow to stern with AUS 216366 most astern boat.
When AUS 216366 was at the mark with distance of slightly more than 1 boat width from it, IRL 211114 sailed between AUS 216366 and the mark.
Contact occurred between the boom of IRL 211114 and back of the sailor and then the mast of AUS 216366 with no damage or injury.
conclusions: IRL 211114 not overlapped with AUS and not in the zone at the time AUS 216366 reached the zone, failed to give AUS 216366 mark-room, and broke RRS 18.2(a)(2).
IRL 211114 did not avoid contact with AUS 216366 even though it was reasonably possible, and broke RRS 14(a).

It was not reasonably possible for AUS 216366 the boat sailing within the mark-room to which she was entitled to avoid contact with IRL 211114 when it became clear that IRL 211114 was not giving mark-room. AUS 216366 did not break RRS 14(a).
